analysis.title: Tesla Inc. (TSLA): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: GS expects investors to view the 3Q26 report positively on progress in autonomy, demand and gross profit. Gross margin beat GS in all three segments. Opex was above GS's estimate, Energy revenue was below, and Optimus is still being iterated, but GS's first take is positive on balance.
Key questions for the call: pace of deployments in physical AI businesses, the trajectory of capex and free cash flow, and margins.

3Q26 revenue was $28,046 mn (down 1% qoq, about flat yoy). That is 4% below GS at $29,330 mn, about in line with the Street (FactSet) at $28,057 mn, and 1% below company-compiled consensus at $28,341 mn.
Total company gross margin including SBC was 19.6%, versus GS 18.5%, company-compiled consensus 17.9% and Street (FactSet) 17.5%. 2Q26 was 16.8% and 3Q25 was 18.0%.
Automotive non-GAAP gross margin (including SBC, excluding regulatory credits) was 18.1%, versus GS 16.3% and Street 16.8%.

EBIT including SBC was about $718 mn (2.6% of sales), below GS at about $1,043 mn (3.6%) and the Street at $1,473 mn (5.3%), and about in line with company-compiled consensus of $721 mn (2.5%). The deck cites higher opex and lower regulatory credit revenue as the main drags, partly offset by better mix and growth in FSD and Services.
Company-reported non-GAAP diluted EPS (excluding SBC and non-cash mark to market) was $0.48, versus GS $0.44 and Street and company-compiled consensus $0.45.

Cash, cash equivalents and investments rose $1.9 bn qoq to $45.4 bn. FCF was $1,531 mn in 3Q. Capex was $4.7 bn versus GS's $8.0 bn estimate. Tesla had previously expected over $25 bn of capex for the year.

FSD active subscribers reached 1.74 mn (up 18% qoq and 67% yoy). FSD attach rate on new vehicle deliveries in North America was above 75%, up from above 55% in 2Q. Tesla also received several European approvals for FSD in the quarter.

Cumulative paid unsupervised robotaxi miles were 3.1 mn as of October 18, up from 1 mn on September 3, 2026 and about 380K at the 2Q call. Cybercab rolled out in Austin. San Antonio and Jacksonville were added to the upcoming cities list alongside Phoenix and Las Vegas.
Optimus began production on high-volume lines in Fremont. Tesla believes the process suits a commercial product but continues to iterate on hardware and manufacturing.
Megafactory Texas started production (Megablock and Megapack). Tesla Semi volume production started in Nevada.
Tesla expects 400 MW of compute by year-end, from about 265 MW now, and started construction on its Austin Fab with equipment commissioning expected in 2027.

Battery availability remains a limiting factor in the global vehicle production ramp. Tesla is working on pack capacity in Berlin, cathode production and lithium refining in Texas, and LFP cells in Nevada for Energy.
Tesla said its passenger vehicle backlog is the highest in four years and its Energy backlog is at a record high.
Energy revenue of $2,881 mn was 23.2% below GS's $3,749 mn estimate. Total Automotive revenue of $20,560 mn was 2.4% below GS and 1.4% above company-compiled consensus.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a 12-month target of $360, based on 150X applied to Q5-Q8E EPS including SBC. The stock closed at $373.71 on 20 Oct 2026, 3.7% above the target.

earnings_insights: Revenue $28,046 mn reported vs GS est $29,330 mn, Street (FactSet) est $28,057 mn, company-compiled consensus est $28,341 mn.
Non-GAAP EPS excluding SBC $0.48 reported vs GS est $0.44, Street est $0.45, company-compiled consensus est $0.45. Non-GAAP EPS including SBC was $0.20 reported vs GS est $0.24.
Total gross margin including SBC 19.6% reported vs GS est 18.5%, Street est 17.5%, company-compiled consensus est 17.9%.
GAAP operating income including SBC $718 mn reported (2.6% margin) vs GS est $1,043 mn, Street est $1,473 mn, company-compiled consensus est $721 mn.
Energy generation and storage revenue $2,881 mn reported vs GS est $3,749 mn and Street est $3,720 mn. Service and other revenue $4,605 mn reported vs GS est $4,518 mn and Street est $4,349 mn.
Regulatory credits were $113 mn reported vs GS est $400 mn.
Vehicle deliveries were 486,532 (Model 3/Y 478,237, other models 8,295), up 1.3% qoq and down 2.1% yoy. Energy deployments were 13.7 GWh, up 1.5% qoq and 9.6% yoy.
GS EPS estimates (including SBC): $0.24 for 3Q26E and $0.31 for 4Q26E. FY26E EPS is $0.82 and FY27E is $1.75.
risk_factors: Downside risks: larger vehicle price cuts than GS expects, more EV competition, a larger tariff impact or adverse government policy, slower EV demand, delays in FSD or 4680, key person risk, the internal control environment, margins, and operational risk from vertical integration.

Upside risks: faster EV adoption or share gain, a stronger macro backdrop for new vehicle sales, earlier product launches, an earlier or larger impact from AI-enabled products (FSD, Optimus, robotaxis), and a smaller tariff impact.
Battery availability is a limiting factor on global vehicle production.
